families.title: Imports and exports
families.row: One static import or export declaration in a source-file section.
families.grouping: Compare adjacent declarations only when their static syntax, role, and section match; preserve source order.
families.nesting: Imported-name lists belong to the declaration cell and do not share axes with the outer declaration unless a future parser policy owns both levels.
families.separation: Comments, side-effect boundaries, blank-line sections, and executable statements separate candidate groups contextually.

families.title: Declarations and assignments
families.row: One declaration or assignment whose name, optional type, equals sign, and value can be bounded losslessly.
families.grouping: Group same-role sibling statements with compatible axes without reordering; the TypeScript declaration-equals detector may identify two rows, but automatic application remains gated by an exact approved rule and proof, while Python tables normally require three.
families.nesting: A supported call or literal-list value may own an independent inner layer; uncertain or multiline values stay opaque or are refused.
families.separation: Ordinary groups are contiguous; blank lines separate current declaration groups, while comments or incompatible statements also end a run.

families.title: Function signatures
families.row: One method or callable signature with a bounded name, parameter envelope, and optional return-type boundary.
families.grouping: Compare sibling signatures of the same declaration role and container; keep overload sets and runtime methods distinct when their roles differ.
families.nesting: Parameters and their defaults are owned by the signature cell; nested function types or destructured parameters require a separate supported policy.
families.separation: Blank lines and non-signature members end current TypeScript runs; decorators and documentation are structural boundaries needing review.

families.title: Calls and chains
families.row: One supported call statement or call-valued declaration, with receiver/callee and an owned argument envelope.
families.grouping: Use the registered TypeScript call kind or the exact Python assigned-call signature; preserve callees, arity, and evaluation order.
families.nesting: Outer call punctuation and each supported inner call/list layer have separate ownership; heterogeneous arguments remain opaque.
families.separation: Comments at member boundaries, incompatible calls, and ordinary blank lines end a run; no statement is moved to create a table.
exclusions: TypeScript type arguments in nested call layers

families.title: Branches and exits
families.row: One bounded guard, case clause, or exit-bearing row in a single control-flow container.
families.grouping: Compare guards only within the same owned block region and preserve all intervening statement order; case clauses use their own kind.
families.nesting: Nested blocks establish independent regions; punctuation inside conditions belongs to the condition cell.
families.separation: Blank lines are contextual: supported TypeScript return regions may span them, while comments, terminal statements, and unsupported guards can break a region.

families.title: Object and type members
families.row: One sibling property, field, enum member, or registration entry with a bounded key/name and value or type.
families.grouping: Group siblings only within the same object, type, class, interface, enum, or supported mapping container and only when their roles match.
families.nesting: Nested object/type values create lower independent tables; outer and inner colons never share an axis.
families.separation: Blank lines split current TypeScript member runs; Python dictionary rows require a compatible contiguous table.

families.title: Arrays and repeated records
families.row: One repeated array element, tuple-like bundle, or object record with corresponding bounded fields.
families.grouping: Require sibling rows with compatible shape, field order, and owned delimiters; preserve record and element order.
families.nesting: Each nested list or record owns an independent layer; only registered literal layers may be decomposed today.
families.separation: Container boundaries always separate groups; comments and heterogeneous elements may split or refuse a candidate depending on language syntax.
exclusions: JSON or YAML public writes before CLI integration and approved presets exist

families.title: Operators and expressions
families.row: One expression-bearing statement whose operands and operator boundary can be identified without changing precedence.
families.grouping: Only group expressions with the same statement role and compatible operator semantics; keep original evaluation and statement order.
families.nesting: Parenthesized, ternary, short-circuit, and nested expressions remain opaque unless a dedicated policy owns that expression level.
families.separation: Blank lines, comments, and changes of operator or statement role are contextual barriers rather than a universal rule.

families.title: Structured documents
families.row: One sibling mapping entry with a parser-owned key, delimiter, and scalar or opaque value.
families.grouping: Compare sibling mapping entries in the same parsed container; preserve key order, duplicates, escapes, indentation, and document boundaries.
families.nesting: Nested mappings, sequences, and flow collections own independent axes and remain opaque to their parent row.
families.separation: JSON container syntax bounds groups; YAML blank lines and comments are contextual and document markers always separate documents.
exclusions: public writes before CLI integration and approved presets exist
